question: The western part of the northern plains is formed by which of the following river systems?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indus and its tributaries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The western part of the northern plains of India is predominantly formed by the river system of the Indus and its tributaries.
 
• The major tributaries of the Indus River include the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej rivers.
 
• These rivers collectively contribute to the fertile plains, making the region agriculturally rich and significant.
 
• The Indus River system plays a crucial role in the irrigation and water supply in the northwestern part of India, particularly in Punjab and Haryana.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus River**

 
 
• The Indus River is one of the longest rivers in the world, stretching over 3,180 km (1,976 miles).
 
• It originates in the Tibetan Plateau in the vicinity of Lake Mansarovar, flowing through Ladakh in India and then into Pakistan before emptying into the Arabian Sea.
 
• The river basin supports a variety of ecosystems and is home to several important cities, including Karachi in Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Tributaries of Indus**
 
 
• The Jhelum River is known for its historical significance and is a major water source for the region of Kashmir.
 
• The Chenab River is the largest tributary of the Indus, providing vital water resources for irrigation and hydroelectricity.
 
• The Ravi River, historically known as the Iravati, flows through the Indian state of Punjab and Pakistan.
 
• The Beas River merges with the Sutlej River, further contributing to the Indus river system.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Importance**
 
 
• The northern plains, formed by the alluvial deposits from these rivers, are among the most fertile agricultural regions in the world.
 
• This area is known as the breadbasket of India due to its high productivity of staple crops like wheat and rice.
